entries.sanskrit:
त्रिंशे तु कायकान्तादि- लालनाकुल-चेतसाम् ।

कामिनां तामसी पापाद् अधोगतिर् उदीर्यते ॥

काल-प्रभाव-वर्णन-पूर्वकं वैराग्याय विचित्र-कर्म-कृतां संसृतिम् अध्याय-त्रयेण प्रपञ्चयति । तस्यैतस्य बलिनः कालस्य । बलिनेति वा पाठः । काल्यमानो विचाल्यमानोऽपि । वायोर् विक्रमं यथा मेघ-पङ्क्तिर् न वेद ॥१॥
word_for_word: of those whose minds are absorbed in pampering the body, spouse, and the like
of sensualists; those driven by desire
with a description of Time’s power preceding it
of those who perform varied actions
or the reading is balinā, “by mighty [Time]”
a bank; a row of clouds
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration:
triṃśe tu kāyakāntādi- lālanākula-cetasām |

kāmināṃ tāmasī pāpād adhogatir udīryate ||

kāla-prabhāva-varṇana-pūrvakaṃ vairāgyāya vicitra-karma-kṛtāṃ saṃsṛtim adhyāya-trayeṇa prapañcayati | tasyaitasya balinaḥ kālasya | balineti vā pāṭhaḥ | kālyamāno vicālyamāno’pi | vāyor vikramaṃ yathā megha-paṅktir na veda ||1||
entries.literal_english: In the thirtieth chapter, the dark downward destination caused by sin is described for sensualists absorbed in pampering the body, spouse, and the like. The commentator says that, with Time’s power described first, he elaborates over three chapters the transmigration of those who perform varied actions, for the sake of detachment. “Of this mighty Time” has the alternative reading “by mighty [Time].” Though harried by Time and shaken, a person does not perceive its force, just as a bank of clouds does not perceive the force of the wind.

entries.sanskrit: विक्रमम् एवाह---यं यम् अर्थं दुःखेन प्रयासेनोपादत्ते आपादयति, तं तम् अर्थं भगवान् कालो धुनोति विनाशयति । यत्-कृते यन्-निमित्तम् ॥२॥
word_for_word: he now explains the force [of Time]
that is, on account of which
entries.literal_english: He now explains Time’s force: whatever object a person acquires with difficulty and effort, the Lord, Time, shakes away and destroys. “For whose sake” means “on account of which.”
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: vikramam evāha---yaṃ yam arthaṃ duḥkhena prayāsenopādatte āpādayati, taṃ tam arthaṃ bhagavān kālo dhunoti vināśayati | yat-kṛte yan-nimittam ||2||

entries.sanskrit: शोके हेतुः, यत् यस्मात् सानुबन्धस्य कलत्रादि-सहितस्य देहस्य सम्बन्धीनि गृहादीनि । वसु द्रव्यम् । अनुक्त-समुच्चयार्थश् च-कारः ॥३॥
word_for_word: of the one with dependents; family ties
of the body accompanied by a wife and others
houses and the like related to it
the particle “ca” adds what has not been stated
entries.literal_english: The reason for grief is this: houses and the like are related to the body that has dependents, including a wife and others. “Vasu” means wealth or property. The particle “ca” adds things not explicitly stated.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: śoke hetuḥ, yat yasmāt sānubandhasya kalatrādi-sahitasya dehasya sambandhīni gṛhādīni | vasu dravyam | anukta-samuccayārthaś ca-kāraḥ ||3||

entries.sanskrit: दुर्मतित्वं दर्शयन् दुःखं प्रपञ्चयति---जन्तुर् इति चतुर्दशभिः ॥४॥
entries.literal_english: While showing the person’s foolishness, the text elaborates his suffering through the fourteen verses beginning “the living being ...”.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: durmatitvaṃ darśayan duḥkhaṃ prapañcayati---jantur iti caturdaśabhiḥ ||4||

entries.sanskrit: नारक्यां नरकाहारादिभिर् जातायाम् ॥५॥
word_for_word: from hellish food and the like
entries.literal_english: “In hellish enjoyment” means enjoyment arising from hellish food and the like.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: nārakyāṃ narakāhārādibhir jātāyām ||5||

entries.sanskrit: निरूढ-मूलं प्रसृत-मनोरथं हृदयं यस्य । बहु मन्यते कृतार्थोऽहम् इति श्लाघते ॥६॥
entries.literal_english: “Whose heart is deeply rooted and whose desires have spread”; he thinks highly of himself and boasts, “I have achieved my ends.”
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: nirūḍha-mūlaṃ prasṛta-manorathaṃ hṛdayaṃ yasya | bahu manyate kṛtārtho’ham iti ślāghate ||6||

entries.sanskrit: उद्वहनाधिना पोषण-चिन्तया ॥७॥
word_for_word: because of anxiety about bearing or supporting
through concern about maintenance or nourishment
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: udvahanādhinā poṣaṇa-cintayā ||7||
entries.literal_english: Ud-vahana-adhinā is explained by poṣaṇa-cintayā: through anxiety about bearing the burden of maintenance.

entries.sanskrit: दुराशयत्वम् आह---आक्षिप्त आत्मा इन्द्रियाणि च यस्य । कया ? असतीनां पुंश्चलीनाम् अपि रहसि रचितया सम्भोगादि-रूपया । मधुर-भाषिणां शिशूनाम् आलापैश् च । सुखवन् मन्यत इत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः ॥८॥ कूटाः वित्त-शाठ्यादि-बहुला धर्मा येषु दुःख-प्रधानेषु ॥९॥
word_for_word: in the form of sexual enjoyment and the like
thus it connects grammatically with what follows
abounding in financial deceit and the like
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: durāśayatvam āha---ākṣipta ātmā indriyāṇi ca yasya | kayā ? asatīnāṃ puṃścalīnām api rahasi racitayā sambhogādi-rūpayā | madhura-bhāṣiṇāṃ śiśūnām ālāpaiś ca | sukhavan manyata ity uttareṇānvayaḥ ||8|| kūṭāḥ vitta-śāṭhyādi-bahulā dharmā yeṣu duḥkha-pradhāneṣu ||9||
entries.literal_english: He explains the corrupt motive: a person whose self and senses are captivated by secret arrangements for sexual enjoyment and the like with unchaste, promiscuous women, and by the chatter of sweet-speaking children, thinks himself happy; this construction connects with what follows. Those practices are deceptive, abound in financial trickery and the like, and are dominated by suffering.

entries.sanskrit: येषां पोषणेनाधो याति तान् पुष्णाति । शेष-भुग् इति भोगोऽपि तस्य दुर्लभ इत्य् अर्थः ॥१०॥
word_for_word: even enjoyment is difficult for him
entries.literal_english: He maintains those by whose maintenance he himself goes downward. The phrase “eats the leftovers” means that even enjoyment is difficult for him.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: yeṣāṃ poṣaṇenādho yāti tān puṣṇāti | śeṣa-bhug iti bhogo’pi tasya durlabha ity arthaḥ ||10||

entries.sanskrit: वार्तायां जीविकायाम् । निःसत्त्वोऽशक्तः । परार्थे पर-स्वे ॥११॥
entries.literal_english: “Vārtā” means livelihood. “Without strength” means incapable. “For another’s sake” means [coveting] another person’s property.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: vārtāyāṃ jīvikāyām | niḥsattvo’śaktaḥ | parārthe para-sve ||11||

entries.sanskrit: अकल्पोऽसमर्थः ॥१२॥
entries.literal_english: “Akalpa” means incapable; unable.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: akalpo’samarthaḥ ||12||

entries.sanskrit: पूर्वं यथाद्रियन्ते तथादरं न कुर्वन्ति । कीनाशाः कृपणाः कृषीवलाः । गो-जरं वृद्धं बलीवर्दम् ॥१३॥
word_for_word: as they used to respect [him] before
they do not show the same respect
entries.literal_english: They do not show him the respect they showed him before. “Kīnāśāḥ” means farmers—miserly cultivators. “Go-jara” means an old bullock.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: pūrvaṃ yathādriyante tathādaraṃ na kurvanti | kīnāśāḥ kṛpaṇāḥ kṛṣīvalāḥ | go-jaraṃ vṛddhaṃ balīvardam ||13||

entries.sanskrit: भ्रियमाणः पुष्यमाणः ॥१४॥ अवमत्यावज्ञयोपन्यस्तं समीपे प्रक्षिप्तम् । गृह-पालः श्वा । आहरन् भुञ्जानः । आमयावी रोगी ॥१५॥
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: bhriyamāṇaḥ puṣyamāṇaḥ ||14|| avamatyāvajñayopanyastaṃ samīpe prakṣiptam | gṛha-pālaḥ śvā | āharan bhuñjānaḥ | āmayāvī rogī ||15||
entries.literal_english: Bhriyamāṇaḥ is explained as puṣyamāṇaḥ: being maintained and nourished. Avamatya means “with contempt”; upanyastam is something placed nearby, that is, thrown down. Gṛha-pālaḥ, “house-guardian,” means a dog. Āharan means bhuñjānaḥ, “eating”; āmayāvī means rogī, “sick.”

entries.sanskrit: उत्तारो बहिर् निर्गत-नेत्रः । कफेन संरुद्धाः नाड्यो मार्ग-भूता यस्य । कास-श्वासाभ्यां कृत आयासो यस्य । घुर-घुर इति शब्दं करोति ॥१६॥
word_for_word: which serve as passages, of whom
entries.literal_english: “Uttāra” means that the eyes protrude outward. His channels, which serve as passages, are blocked by phlegm. He is distressed by coughing and difficult breathing, and makes a gurgling sound.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: uttāro bahir nirgata-netraḥ | kaphena saṃruddhāḥ nāḍyo mārga-bhūtā yasya | kāsa-śvāsābhyāṃ kṛta āyāso yasya | ghura-ghura iti śabdaṃ karoti ||16||

entries.sanskrit: परिवीतः परिवेष्टितः । वाच्यमणो बन्धो तातेत्य् आहूयमानः ॥१७॥
word_for_word: being addressed [as recorded in the source]
entries.literal_english: “Parivīta” means surrounded. His grieving relatives surround him and call out, “O kinsman! O father!”
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: parivītaḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ | vācyamaṇo bandho tātety āhūyamānaḥ ||17||

entries.sanskrit: अस्त-धीर् नष्ट-मतिः ॥१८॥
entries.literal_english: “Asta-dhīḥ” means that his mind has failed; his understanding is lost.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: asta-dhīr naṣṭa-matiḥ ||18||

entries.sanskrit: मृतस्य पुण्य-पापाभ्यां द्वे गती । तत्र पाप-गतिम् आह---यम-दूताव् इत्य्-आदि यावत् समाप्ति । स-रभसं स-क्रोधम् ईक्षणं ययोस् तौ दृष्ट्वा ॥१९॥
word_for_word: there he describes the sinful destination
beginning with “the two messengers of Yama”
seeing those two, whose [glances are so]
entries.literal_english: For a dead person there are two destinations, according to merit and sin. Here the sinful destination is described, beginning with “the two messengers of Yama” and continuing to the end. Seeing those two, whose glances are fierce and angry, he is terrified.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: mṛtasya puṇya-pāpābhyāṃ dve gatī | tatra pāpa-gatim āha---yama-dūtāv ity-ādi yāvat samāpti | sa-rabhasaṃ sa-krodham īkṣaṇaṃ yayos tau dṛṣṭvā ||19||

entries.sanskrit: आवृत्य निरुध्य ॥२०॥
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: āvṛtya nirudhya ||20||
entries.literal_english: Āvṛtya means having enclosed or covered; nirudhya means having restrained or confined.

entries.sanskrit: तयोस् तर्जनैर् निर्भिन्नं हृदयं यस्य । आर्तः संश् चलतीति द्वितीयेनान्वयः ॥२१॥ क्षुत्-तृड्भ्यां परीतो व्याप्तः । तप्ता वालुका यस्मिन् । निर्गत आश्रमो विश्राम-स्थानम् उदकं च यस्मिन् ॥२२॥
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: tayos tarjanair nirbhinnaṃ hṛdayaṃ yasya | ārtaḥ saṃś calatīti dvitīyenānvayaḥ ||21|| kṣut-tṛḍbhyāṃ parīto vyāptaḥ | taptā vālukā yasmin | nirgata āśramo viśrāma-sthānam udakaṃ ca yasmin ||22||
entries.literal_english: His heart is pierced by the threats of those two [messengers]. Being distressed, he moves on; this is connected with the second statement. He is overwhelmed by hunger and thirst. The road has burning sand and lacks both a resting place and water.

entries.sanskrit: यम-सादनं नीतो भवति ॥२३॥
entries.literal_english: He is brought to the abode of Yama.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: yama-sādanaṃ nīto bhavati ||23||

entries.sanskrit: तत्रैव विशेषम् आह---**अध्वनः** सम्बन्धिनां **योजनानां नवतिं नव** च **सहस्राणि** पापाधिक्ये **द्वाभ्यां वा नीतः** सन् ॥२४॥
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: tatraiva viśeṣam āha---**adhvanaḥ** sambandhināṃ **yojanānāṃ navatiṃ nava** ca **sahasrāṇi** pāpādhikye **dvābhyāṃ vā nītaḥ** san ||24||
entries.literal_english: He specifies the distance: ninety-nine thousand yojanas of road. When the sin is greater, the person is brought in two [muhūrtas]. Here dvābhyām is an alternative duration—two muhūrtas—not “by two” messengers.

entries.sanskrit: यातनाः सङ्क्षेपतो दर्शयति चतुर्भिः । आदीपनं प्रज्वलनं प्राप्नोति । स्वेन कृत्तम् अन्येन वा कृत्तं छिन्नं यत् स्वस्य मांसं तस्य भक्षणम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२५॥
word_for_word: that cut flesh of his own
entries.literal_english: In four verses the text briefly describes the torments. Ādīpana means setting alight; prajvalana means blazing. He undergoes the eating of his own flesh, whether cut by himself or by another.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: yātanāḥ saṅkṣepato darśayati caturbhiḥ | ādīpanaṃ prajvalanaṃ prāpnoti | svena kṛttam anyena vā kṛttaṃ chinnaṃ yat svasya māṃsaṃ tasya bhakṣaṇam ity arthaḥ ||25||

entries.sanskrit: आत्मनो वैशसं पीडाम् ॥२६॥
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: ātmano vaiśasaṃ pīḍām ||26||
entries.literal_english: Vaiśasam means anguish or torment; pīḍām means pain or affliction suffered by the self.

entries.sanskrit: भिदापनं भेद-प्रापणम् ॥२७॥
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: bhidāpanaṃ bheda-prāpaṇam ||27||
entries.literal_english: Bhidāpanam means causing division—that is, bringing about separation.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara Svāmī explicitly gives no commentary here in the pinned source.
entries.source_note: The pinned source explicitly marks Śrīdhara Svāmī and Viśvanātha Cakravartin as not commenting at 3.30.28.

entries.sanskrit: न चैतद् असम्भावितम् अत्रापि दृश्यमानत्वाद् इत्य् आह---अतैवेति ॥२९॥
word_for_word: because it is seen here too
entries.literal_english: The text says, “Right here”: this is not impossible, because it is seen here too.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: na caitad asambhāvitam atrāpi dṛśyamānatvād ity āha---ataiveti ||29||

entries.sanskrit: उभयं कुटुम्बं स्वं देहं च ॥३०॥
entries.literal_english: “Both” refers to the family and one’s own body.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: ubhayaṃ kuṭumbaṃ svaṃ dehaṃ ca ||30||

entries.sanskrit: पापार्जितं धनं भुञ्जते बहवः, कर्तैन नरकं यातीत्य् आह---एक इति । भूत-द्रोहेण यद् भृतं तत् स्थूलं स्व-कलेवरम् इहैव हित्वा । कुशलाद् इतरत् पापं तद् एव पाथेयं भोग्यं यस्य ॥३१॥
word_for_word: the doer alone goes to hell [source reads “कर्तैन”]
that gross body of his own
for whom that alone is the provision to be experienced
entries.literal_english: Many people enjoy wealth acquired through sin, but the doer alone goes to hell. The gross body, nourished by harming living beings, is left here. For that person, sin—the opposite of merit—is the very provision to be experienced on the journey. The pinned source reads “कर्तैन”; this gloss follows the apparent sense “the doer alone,” without changing the Sanskrit transcription.
entries.source_note: Pinned source text retained, including apparent transcription “कर्तैन”; the English gloss gives the contextual sense “the doer alone” without silently changing the Sanskrit.
transliteration: pāpārjitaṃ dhanaṃ bhuñjate bahavaḥ, kartaina narakaṃ yātīty āha---eka iti | bhūta-droheṇa yad bhṛtaṃ tat sthūlaṃ sva-kalevaram ihaiva hitvā | kuśalād itarat pāpaṃ tad eva pātheyaṃ bhogyaṃ yasya ||31||

entries.sanskrit: ननु पापम् अपि विहाय गच्छतु तत्राह---दैवेनेति । तस्य कुटुम्ब-पोषणस्य शमलं पापं दैवनेनेश्वरेण प्रापितं भुङ्क्ते ॥३२॥
word_for_word: by fate—that is, by the Lord
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: nanu pāpam api vihāya gacchatu tatrāha---daiveneti | tasya kuṭumba-poṣaṇasya śamalaṃ pāpaṃ daivaneneśvareṇa prāpitaṃ bhuṅkte ||32||
entries.literal_english: One might object: “Then let him go, leaving even the sin behind.” The passage answers with “by fate”: he undergoes the stain—the sin—of maintaining his family, which has been brought upon him by the Lord.

entries.sanskrit: ननु कुटुम्ब-पोषणं विहितम् एव तत्राह---केवलेनेति । तमसो नरकस्य चरमं पदं स्थानम् ॥३३॥
entries.literal_english: One may object that maintaining a family is indeed prescribed. The text answers with “alone”: hell is the final station, the place of darkness.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: nanu kuṭumba-poṣaṇaṃ vihitam eva tatrāha---kevaleneti | tamaso narakasya caramaṃ padaṃ sthānam ||33||

entries.sanskrit: पुनर् मनुष्य-शरीर-प्राप्ति-प्रकारम् आह---नर-लोकस्य मनुष्य-देहस्य प्राप्तेर् अधस्ताद् अर्वाग् यावत्यो यातनाः । आदि-शब्देन श्व-सूकरादि-योनयश् च यास्ताः सर्वाः क्रमेण संप्राप्य भोगेन क्षीण-पापः शुचिः सन्न् अत्र पुनर् नरत्वं प्राप्नोतीत्य् अर्थः ॥३४॥
word_for_word: he again describes how a human body is regained
the torments below it, to whatever extent
dog, pig, and other births too
शुचिः सन्न् अत्र पुनर् नरत्वं प्राप्नोति
being purified, he regains human life here
entries.literal_english: He again describes how a human body is regained. The torments and other births below human life include dog, pig, and other species. Having passed through all of them in sequence and exhausted his sin by experiencing them, the person becomes purified and regains human life here.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block keyed to pinned merged source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase glosses follow the source.
transliteration: punar manuṣya-śarīra-prāpti-prakāram āha---nara-lokasya manuṣya-dehasya prāpter adhastād arvāg yāvatyo yātanāḥ | ādi-śabdena śva-sūkarādi-yonayaś ca yāstāḥ sarvāḥ krameṇa saṃprāpya bhogena kṣīṇa-pāpaḥ śuciḥ sann atra punar naratvaṃ prāpnotīty arthaḥ ||34||
